transcript.answer: No. Otto refuses to let a tool take a customer number in its input schema. `enforceNoCustomerInput` in `apps/api/src/tools/toolAuth.ts` (FR-034) checks each tool definition's `inputSchema` property names against a customer/company/account identifier pattern. If one matches, it throws an error, so the tool cannot register. ADR-001 says `registerTools` applies this check at any depth of the schema. A test, `apps/api/test/customerBoundary.test.ts`, walks every registered tool to confirm none declare such a field. The customer number comes from the verified login token's `customer_number` claim on each call, not from anything the model supplies. For example, `get_booking_status` takes only `booking_reference`.

judgements.reason: The answer says no and covers the gold's essentials: registerTools refuses customer, company or account identifiers at any depth, and a test walks every registered definition. It omits only the English/Danish spelling detail, and nothing in it contradicts the gold.
